dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?
Good afternoon, Tony. This is Ileana Figueroa. I'm at 299 Van Zandt Avenue, up in the North End. I have a question about my water and sewer bill.
Sure thing, Mrs. Figueroa. What's going on with it?
Well, first, I have to say, your phone menu. Press one, press two, I half expected Bob Barker to come on and tell me what I'd won. It was a game show.
We hear that. Sorry about the maze. You got to the right place, anyway.

I did, eventually. So. A new meter was installed at my house last month. A man came, he was in and out in maybe forty minutes. Fine. Now I get this bill and it looks off to me. It's quite a bit higher than what I'm used to.
Okay. Do you have the bill in front of you? Let's look at what it shows.
I do. It's right here. The usage line says forty-one units. My old bills ran around eighteen, twenty. It's just me in this house, Tony. I'm not running a laundromat.

Understood. A unit on your bill is one hundred cubic feet of water, so it's a measure of volume. Forty-one is a big jump from twenty. Let me pull up the account. Can you give me the account number off the top of the bill?
It's the number up in the right corner. Hold on. Four, four, seven, one, zero, three. Is that enough?
That works, I've got it. Okay, I see the meter change on the account last month. The old meter has a final read, and the new one starts fresh. Let me look at how the dates line up.
Take your time. I'm retired, I have all day. Well, I have until my one-thirty program.

[pause] Alright. So this bill covers a longer period than usual. It's about sixty days, not the regular billing stretch, because of the meter swap. That could explain part of it. But even so, forty-one is high for sixty days if you normally use eighteen in a period.
That's what I figured. So is it the meter, or is it me?

I can't tell you from here, honestly. It could be a meter that's reading wrong, it could be a leak on your side, like a toilet running, or it could be the read itself. Do you know if your toilets run on after you flush?
No. I checked that already. My late husband, he was Navy, he'd have my head if I let a toilet run. I did the dye thing with the food coloring. Nothing.
Good, that's the right test. Then the next step is a meter check. We can send someone out to test that the new meter is reading accurately and look at the read on site.
Good. And I want to dispute the charge formally, too. What do I do for that? Is there a form, or do I write a letter? I want it on paper.

You can do it in writing. A letter to the utilities billing office works. Put your name, the address, the account number, the bill date, and say that you're disputing the charge and why. Mention the new meter and the date it was installed. You can drop it off here at City Hall or mail it.
Mail it to City Hall, same address as always?
Yes, to the Utilities billing office at City Hall in Newport. Address is on the top of your bill as well.
Alright. Does the dispute stop the bill from going late? I don't want a penalty on top of everything.

Good question. I'll put a note on the account right now saying you've questioned the bill and requested a meter test. I can't promise how the office handles the due date, but the note will be there, and the letter will back it up.

Fine. Now, my daughter helps me with the bills. She's got a better head for the computer and the paperwork than I do these days. She'd like to be authorized to talk to you folks on my behalf. How do we do that?

We'd need something from you in writing authorizing her. A short signed note works. Her full name, her phone number, the account or address, and that she's allowed to discuss and handle the billing. You can include that in the same letter if you like.
The same envelope. That's efficient. So, one letter: dispute, plus permission for her.
Exactly. I'd keep them as two clearly labeled paragraphs so nobody misses either one. And keep a copy for yourself.
Of course. I kept every carbon copy for forty years of Navy moves. Now, the meter test. When would somebody come?
I'll put in the request now. They usually call first to set a window. Is this number, the one you're calling from, the best one?
Yes, it's 401-555-0171. That's the landline. If I don't answer, leave a message. I'm not always by the phone.
Got it, 401-555-0171. And will someone be home to let them in? Is the meter inside?
It's in the cellar, by the stairs. I'll be here, or my daughter will.
Perfect. I've got the request logged along with the note about the dispute. Anything else I can do for you today?
No, I think that covers it. Let me just repeat. Letter to City Hall, with the dispute and the authorization for my daughter, meter test request is in, and somebody calls me.
That's it exactly.
Thank you, Tony. You were clear. Better than the menu.
I'll take that. You have a good afternoon, Mrs. Figueroa.
You too. Goodbye.
